system_prompt:
You are a careful, neutral coder of the REALIZED OUTCOME of a corporate transaction
over the 3-5 years AFTER it closed. You are given ONE evidence slice assembled from
public primary sources (financial filings, reputable press) that describes ONLY the
post-deal trajectory -- how the combined company actually fared. You are
DELIBERATELY NOT shown how the deal was structured at closing (what transferred and
what did not), and you must NOT speculate about the deal's structure. Code STRICTLY
the documented realized outcome. If the slice does not let you determine a field,
you MUST return "uncertain" -- never guess, never infer from outside knowledge.

Emit a single structured record with these fields.

C. FAILURE-PATHWAY INCIDENCE -- code strictly from the DOCUMENTED OUTCOME at the
3-5 year horizon. A pathway is a REALIZED DISRUPTION OVER TIME, not a structural
property of the deal.
  p4_pathway: Is there documented disruption specifically at the product/process
    interface (the acquired product could not be aligned with the operating
    processes over time; product-line/operations incoherence realized after the
    deal)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented; uncertain.
  p5_pathway: Is there documented fracture specifically at the process/organization
    interface (operations vs people/management/culture; integration of operations
    broke against the organization over time)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented;
    uncertain.
  t1_archetype: Is there documented incoherence in the controlling-intent archetype
    itself as it played out (e.g. an announced "merger of equals" that operated as
    one-sided dominance)? A channel SEPARATE from the product/process and
    process/organization pathways. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.
  t2_model: Is there documented incompatibility of the two business models
    (value-capture logics that could not be reconciled over time)? A channel
    SEPARATE from the pathways above. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.

D. performance_metric: the single best-documented post-deal outcome scalar in the
   slice (e.g. "divested 80.1% after ~108 months", "~$99bn goodwill write-down",
   "no divestiture; assets retained"). One short phrase. If none, "not documented".

rationale: 2-4 sentences citing the slice lines that drove your p4_pathway and
p5_pathway codes specifically. Cite ONLY realized-outcome evidence; do NOT reason
about how the deal was structured at closing.

Emit ONLY the structured record. Code conservatively: absence of documented
evidence for a pathway is 0 (not-documented); inability to determine is "uncertain".

# Outcome sub-dossier — Nationstar Mortgage LLC proposed Chapter 11 asset acquisition of Residential Capital, LLC servicing assets, realized record

> EVIDENTIARY STANDARD: every factual line ends with a `[SRC: <SEC accession / URL>]`
> tag pointing to a public primary source. A fact that cannot be so sourced is written
> `[UNVERIFIED]` and is never guessed. This sub-dossier records ONLY the realized fate of
> the transaction and its record over the fixed outcome window. It contains no information
> about how the transaction was structured. Outcome window fixed at construction:
> Nationstar Mortgage Holdings Inc.'s realized record for fiscal years 2015–2017 (the fixed
> ~3–5-year window after the ~2012 event), with the realized fate of the transaction itself
> sourced to Nationstar's contemporaneous fiscal-year-2012 annual report.

## Realized fate of the transaction
- During 2012 Nationstar pursued a potential acquisition of the mortgage servicing rights and other assets of a financial services company in bankruptcy and received the right to a break-up fee in the event that it did not win the bankruptcy auction for those assets. [SRC: SEC accession 0001520566-13-000021, Form 10-K for fiscal year ended December 31, 2012]
- Nationstar "were not the highest bidder in the auction" and did not win the bankruptcy auction for those assets; it subsequently received the break-up fee. [SRC: SEC accession 0001520566-13-000021, Form 10-K for fiscal year ended December 31, 2012]
- The transaction therefore did not consummate: no ownership boundary was crossed and Nationstar did not acquire the servicing rights, platforms or assets it had sought. [SRC: SEC accession 0001520566-13-000021, Form 10-K for fiscal year ended December 31, 2012]

## Realized outcome scalar over the fixed record
- The single best-documented realized scalar attributable to the transaction is a break-up fee recorded as $15.6 million of contract termination fees for the year ended December 31, 2012, recorded net of the portion payable to Nationstar's co-investment partner in the potential acquisition; Nationstar recognized no contract termination fees in 2011 or 2010. [SRC: SEC accession 0001520566-13-000021, Form 10-K for fiscal year ended December 31, 2012]
- Because the acquisition did not close, there is no acquired-business outcome scalar (net income/loss, goodwill or asset write-down, impairment, or divestiture) attributable to this transaction; the $15.6 million contract termination fee is the realized item, reported as other income. [SRC: SEC accession 0001520566-13-000021, Form 10-K for fiscal year ended December 31, 2012]

## Record over the fixed 3–5-year window
- Nationstar Mortgage Holdings Inc. remained a public registrant and continued to file annual reports through the window (e.g., the Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2015). [SRC: SEC accession 0001628280-16-012098, Form 10-K for fiscal year ended December 31, 2015]
- Nationstar's Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2015 (within the fixed window) contains no reference to "ResCap" or "Residential Capital" anywhere in its business description, segment disclosures, or financial statements — i.e., the proposed acquisition produced no acquired servicing business, platform, goodwill, impairment, or divestiture in Nationstar's operations within the window. [SRC: SEC accession 0001628280-16-012098, Form 10-K for fiscal year ended December 31, 2015]

## Outcome coding note
- Because the transaction was never consummated (no ownership boundary was crossed), there is no post-close acquired-business trajectory to report at the product/process or process/organization interfaces; that trajectory is not applicable (no acquired business). This is a documented non-consummation, primary-sourced to Nationstar's fiscal-year-2012 annual report and confirmed by the absence of any acquired-business record in the in-window fiscal-year-2015 annual report — not a data gap. [SRC: SEC accession 0001520566-13-000021, Form 10-K for fiscal year ended December 31, 2012] [SRC: SEC accession 0001628280-16-012098, Form 10-K for fiscal year ended December 31, 2015]

## Outcome summary (realized record only)
- The proposed acquisition of the bankrupt financial services company's mortgage servicing rights, platforms and related assets did not close: Nationstar was not the highest bidder in the bankruptcy auction, did not win the assets, and instead received a break-up fee recorded as $15.6 million of contract termination fees (net of the co-investment partner's portion) for the year ended December 31, 2012; its in-window fiscal-year-2015 annual report shows no such acquired business within its operations, consistent with a transaction that was never consummated. [SRC: SEC accession 0001520566-13-000021, Form 10-K for fiscal year ended December 31, 2012] [SRC: SEC accession 0001628280-16-012098, Form 10-K for fiscal year ended December 31, 2015]

[SLICE END]
